editorial:
Tim and Ted Templeton are all grown up now, and they have drifted apart. Tim is a stay-at-home dad, while Ted is a busy businessman. But when a new boss baby shows up with a mission, the brothers are forced to team up again. This time, they drink a special formula that turns them back into kids so they can go undercover at a school run by an evil genius. The movie is bright, loud, and packed with jokes that kids will love. The animation is colorful and the action moves fast, so there is never a dull moment. The story is simple enough for little ones to follow, but there are enough silly gags to keep parents smiling too.

The voice cast does a solid job, especially Alec Baldwin as the boss baby and James Marsden as Tim. The pacing is quick, though some jokes feel a bit rushed. The villain is fun but not very scary, which is perfect for family viewing. If you enjoyed the first movie, you will have a good time here. It is not a masterpiece, but it is a solid pick for movie night.
endingExplained: In the final act, you watch Tim and Ted discover that Dr. Armstrong plans to erase all parents' memories so kids can rule the world. You see the brothers stop his plan by using the anti-aging formula to turn him into a baby. With the villain defeated, you watch Tim and Ted finally reconnect as brothers and fathers. Ted realizes family matters more than work, and Tim learns to trust his kids. The movie ends with the Templeton family closer than ever, ready for their next adventure together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family comedies and silly adventures.
